title: Your body rule
hookLine: one page for the body: Francis called his body Brother Ass, and at the end asked it to forgive him
tomorrow: the wedding night everyone feared: what did Tobias do first?

lines: FRANCIS FASTS AND SLEEPS ON THE GROUND.
cards: Some people talk to their body like a boss to a worker who's slacking: come on, push through. Francis of Assisi did something like that for years.

He fasted hard, slept on the ground, wore rough cloth, and called his body Brother Ass, a donkey to be driven hard and fed little. Near the end of his life, sick and worn out, he said something very different to it.

teach.b: His early biographer, Thomas of Celano, tells it. Francis admitted he had sinned against Brother Body, and asked it to forgive him. Rejoice, he told it, and forgive me.
Notice the word that stayed: brother. Even the donkey was a brother. Francis could be fierce with his body, but at the end he spoke to it as a companion he'd driven too hard.
That's a Christian teaching older than Francis.
Paul writes to the church at Corinth: "know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you."
In Paul's picture, the body isn't a shell the soul wears. It's a dwelling place. In Christian worship, the body kneels and stands, fasts and feasts: it's part of the prayer.
Francis's late apology sits easily beside that old verse.
So here's the week, gathered. Sleep first, like Jesus in the stern. Move daily, with the grain, like Cook Ding's knife.
Eat with care, blessing when full. Breathe, with something for the breath to carry. Here I am, from the feet up.
Rest, the bow unstrung. Care, the rope and the trust.
One page for the body is a way of never needing to say sorry to it at the end.

how: Christians speak of the body as a temple of the Holy Spirit, and Franciscans remember Francis calling it Brother Body. A personal rule of life often has a short page for the body: sleep, movement, food, breath, rest and care.

a strict plan to change how your body looks by summer
one page of small practices for the body, sleep to care

games.q: a friend's body rule is "no sleep till the project's done, then crash." what does Francis's ending suggest?
o: the body is a brother: Francis asked its pardon for driving it too hard.
push on: saints are remembered for ignoring the body.
the body doesn't matter much to a spiritual life either way.
games.why: Francis drove Brother Ass hard for years, then asked Brother Body to forgive him. He never stopped calling it brother.

practice: Take one page and write a short line for each: sleep, movement, food, breath, scan, rest, care. Keep each line small enough to keep. Then sit with the page on your lap, both hands resting on it, for the rest of the time.

wordCard.voice: Your body rule: one page for the body, sleep to care, written for a brother, not a donkey.

orig.note: Greek: temple, sanctuary. Paul's word in "your body is the temple."
